solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Some hippopotamuses provoke mirth

indicators.note: 'some' of a word is only a portion of it, so the letters sit inside the following word

parts.note: the run of letters in the middle of this long word

explanation.surface: A herd of hippos doing something comical enough to make onlookers laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit in hippopot-AMUSE-s; 'Some' says take only a part of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To amuse someone is to entertain them and cause laughter, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Perhaps Berber in Barnet area is a silly jerk

indicators.note: something silly is muddled and nonsensical, so the letters it describes are jumbled

parts.note: Barnet is Cockney rhyming slang for hair (Barnet Fair), and an afro is a hairstyle
A is the standard abbreviation for area
these two short words are rearranged
a tic is an involuntary jerk or twitch

explanation.surface: A North African visiting the London suburb of Barnet acting like a clumsy fool.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnet is a north London district, but here it is rhyming slang: 'Barnet Fair' means hair. Berber is a language family member, hence 'Perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Berber languages belong to the large Afro-Asiatic family, so Berber is one example of that grouping.

clue.text: Lower parts unclothed

indicators.note: removing clothes strips away the outside, so the outer letters go

parts.note: to sunder is to split apart, so sunders means parts

explanation.surface: A modest note about the bits of a body left bare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parts' looks like a noun for body parts but is a verb; strip the first and last letters of its synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Under and lower both describe something positioned beneath, as in the under jaw or lower jaw.

clue.text: Serious, outspoken book about retired president, winner of Nobel Prize

indicators.note: outspoken means spoken out loud, so a word is given by its sound

parts.note: earnest means serious, and the first name sounds the same
Ruth is a book of the Old Testament

indicators.note: to retire is to go back, so the short word goes backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Gerald Ford was a US president

explanation.surface: A sober, frank biography of an ex-president who won the Nobel Prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' seems to describe the president, but it turns the word for 'about' round. The physicist won the 1908 Nobel Prize for Chemistry.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Zealand-born physicist who split the atom received a Nobel award, so he is one such laureate.

clue.text: Briefly support a SE Asian fish product

indicators.note: said briefly, a word is cut short and loses its last letter

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
taken as written
a Lao is a native of Laos in South-East Asia

explanation.surface: Endorsing, in a few words, some fish-based export from South-East Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface ties the fish product to Asia, but bacalao is the salted cod of Spain and Portugal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacalao is dried salted cod, a preserved food made from fish.

clue.text: Cheer for female act in show of boldness

parts.note: brava is the shout of approval for a female performer
to do is to act

explanation.surface: Applauding a woman's daring performance on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Bravo is for a man, brava for a woman, so 'for female' fixes the ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravado is a swaggering display of courage, often put on to impress others.

clue.text: Content of seed bed beguiled after years

indicators.note: in a down answer, coming after means sitting below, so the order is fixed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
Y is the abbreviation for years
to lead someone on is to beguile or deceive them

explanation.surface: A seed bed's contents tempting a gardener after years of waiting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seed bed' reads as one gardening phrase, but 'seed' belongs to the definition and 'bed' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A cotyledon is the embryonic leaf stored within a seed, part of what the seed holds.

clue.text: Peculiar lens adjusted for astronomical event

indicators.note: something adjusted has been altered and rearranged into a new set-up

parts.note: the letters as printed

explanation.surface: An odd telescope lens recalibrated so an astronomer can watch something in the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: The lens fits the astronomy picture, which hides that 'Peculiar lens' is just the letter supply.
explanation.definitionFit: When the Earth passes between Sun and Moon its shadow darkens the Moon, a sky phenomenon.

clue.text: Trip going around bucket, causing flood

indicators.note: to go around something is to surround it, so one word encloses another

parts.note: an outing is a trip
to bucket down is to pour with rain

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles round a bucket and knocks it over, flooding the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trip' suggests stumbling, but it is an excursion; 'bucket' is a verb, as in rain bucketing down.
explanation.definitionFit: An outpouring is a great gush or stream, much like a flood of water or emotion.

clue.text: Robs stoned mariners

parts.note: stoned means high on drugs
jack is an old word for a sailor, as in jack tar

explanation.surface: Drugged-up sailors carrying out a robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the less common spelling of hijacks, built from the two-part phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To highjack is to seize goods or a vehicle in transit, a form of robbery.

clue.text: About to stalk female bird

indicators.note: a stalker follows behind, so this short word comes after the other

parts.note: her is the female pronoun
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: Someone about to creep up on a female bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' looks like 'on the point of', but 'About' gives a word and 'to stalk' places it behind the female.
explanation.definitionFit: A heron is a long-legged wading fowl, fittingly a bird that stalks fish in shallow water.

clue.text: Early years of Liberal doctor raised by mobster

indicators.note: in a down answer, raising something lifts it so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal
to doctor something is to rig or tamper with it
a hood, short for hoodlum, is a gangster

explanation.surface: The childhood of a Liberal-voting physician brought up by a gangster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is a verb meaning falsify, not a physician, and 'raised' means reversed, not brought up.
explanation.definitionFit: Girlhood is the period of a woman's life when she was young, her youthful time.

clue.text: In France I go with priest

parts.note: je is French for I
colours that go together suit each other

explanation.surface: A traveller in France announcing they will travel with a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go with' reads as accompany, but 'go' alone means match, and 'with' simply joins it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jesuit is a member of the Society of Jesus, a Catholic order whose members are often ordained clergy.

clue.text: Spooner's deer track in Clydesdale?

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of pairs of words

parts.note: a hart is a male deer and a course is a track; swap the first sounds

explanation.surface: A trail left by deer through a valley in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Clydesdale is a Scottish valley, but here it is the heavy horse breed named after it; the question mark flags it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Clydesdale is a powerful draught breed, a classic example of an animal used to pull heavy wagons.

clue.text: Old creature is half-cut and goes unsteadily into the Bull

indicators.note: going into something means ending up inside it
cutting a word in half keeps only one of its two halves

parts.note: the second half of this two-letter word

indicators.note: something moving unsteadily wobbles out of its proper order

parts.note: the four letters are rearranged
Taurus is the zodiac sign of the Bull

explanation.surface: A drunk staggering into a pub called the Bull, described unkindly as an old creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-cut' is British slang for drunk, which suits the pub, but here it means take half of 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The stegosaurus was a plated dinosaur of the Jurassic, an animal from millions of years ago.

clue.text: Jobless socialist worker possibly hoarding unlimited funds

indicators.note: to hoard is to keep stored away inside, so one part holds another

parts.note: a red is a socialist, and a worker ant is one kind of ant

indicators.note: without limits means without its boundaries, so the end letters are dropped

parts.note: the inner letters of the word

explanation.surface: An unemployed left-wing labourer suspected of stockpiling money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Socialist Worker' looks like the newspaper or a party member; 'worker' is an insect, and 'possibly' says an ant is just one kind of worker.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain, being made redundant means losing a job because the post was cut, so it means out of work.

clue.text: Managed Habitat order book

parts.note: order and nature both mean kind or sort, as in 'of that order'
to book a table is to reserve it

explanation.surface: Someone ran an order book for the Habitat furniture shop.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital H suggests the British home-furnishings chain Habitat, and 'order book' reads as one business phrase; both are split.
explanation.definitionFit: A nature reserve is protected land deliberately looked after for wildlife, so it is a cared-for home for animals and plants.

clue.text: Lacking self-discipline, Australia's opener picked up more nuts

definitions.note: the answer is a noun for the state of lacking self-control

indicators.note: an opener comes at the start, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word

indicators.note: sounds picked up are caught by the ear, so a word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: nuts means crazy, so more nuts is crazier

explanation.surface: An undisciplined Australian opening batsman catching yet more nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the opener starts the batting, so the surface is a fielding scene; 'picked up' signals a sound-alike. Acrasia is pronounced like 'a crazier' in non-rhotic speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrasia is a philosophical term for weakness of will, acting against one's better judgement through lack of control.

clue.text: A way to stop crackpot, a bit of a pig

indicators.note: to stop a hole is to plug it, so one piece is pushed inside the other

parts.note: a loon is a crazy person
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way
taken as written

explanation.surface: Calling someone a bit of a pig is one way to silence an eccentric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit of a pig' sounds like an insult, but it is literal: a lardoon is a strip of pork fat.
explanation.definitionFit: A lardoon, also spelt lardon, is a small strip of bacon or pork fat, literally a piece cut from a pig.

clue.text: "Ah well", she sighs, missing sons and house

indicators.note: something missing has gone, so these letters are removed

parts.note: the letters as printed
S is the abbreviation for son, and every one of them goes
HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A woman sighing wistfully about her absent sons and lost home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sons' is plural, so all three S's go from the two words, and then the abbreviation for house is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Heigh-ho is a resigned exclamation of weariness or acceptance, used exactly as one says 'oh well'.

clue.text: A medal that's for those with room for improvement?

definitions.text: A medal that's for those with room for improvement?

parts.words: A medal that's for those with room for improvement?
parts.note: surface reading: an award given to people who still have scope to do better
setter's reading: a medal is an honour of a kind, and the room is a literal room being smartened up inside

explanation.walkthrough: 'Room for improvement' is an idiom for falling short; read literally it is a room someone wants to do up, and a medal is another word for an honour.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both the trade of furnishing and painting rooms and, punningly, an award given on the inside.

clue.text: Then woman leaves, and seamen, heading off in cutters

indicators.note: when someone leaves they are gone, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: taken as written
hen is informal for a woman, especially in Scotland

indicators.note: with its head off, a word loses its first letter

parts.note: sailors are seamen

explanation.surface: A woman walks out, and then so do the sailors, setting off in their small boats.
explanation.walkthrough: Cutters look like boats in a naval scene, but they are people who cut cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailor's job is cutting cloth to make garments, so a tailor is a cutter by trade.

clue.text: Quite small person, completely unknown

parts.note: a tot is a small child
all means wholly or completely, as in all alone
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A rather tiny individual nobody has ever heard of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite small' reads as one phrase, but 'Quite' alone is the definition, in its sense of fully.
explanation.definitionFit: Quite can mean absolutely or wholly, as in 'quite right', the same as totally.

clue.text: Excellent case of rioja brought back for a song

indicators.note: bringing something back returns it the way it came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, with the 1 read as the letter I

indicators.note: a case is the outside casing, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the wine

explanation.surface: A first-rate crate of Spanish red returned in exchange for a song.
explanation.walkthrough: Rioja is a Spanish red wine; 'case' reads as a crate of bottles but means only its outside letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo vocal piece in an opera, a particular kind of song.

clue.text: No charge imposed on duke by stern regulatory system

indicators.note: in a down answer, a thing imposed on another is placed above it

parts.note: no is a negative answer
a fee is a charge
D is the abbreviation for duke
the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A duke escapes a fine, thanks to a strict system of rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No charge' reads as free of cost, but 'No' gives one piece and 'charge' another; 'stern' is the noun, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Negative feedback is a control loop in which an output reduces its own cause, keeping a process stable.

clue.text: Three-legged race

parts.note: surface reading: the sports-day race where partners run with two legs tied together
setter's reading: an endurance contest made of three legs, or stages, of swimming, cycling and running

explanation.walkthrough: A leg is also a stage of a relay or journey, so the contest has three stages rather than three limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: This multisport event consists of three successive sections, swimming then cycling then running, each one a leg.

clue.text: Laughing out loud, went ahead and sprawled

parts.note: LOL is the texting abbreviation for laughing out loud
to lead is to go ahead of others

explanation.surface: Someone guffawed, carried on regardless and stretched out on the sofa.
explanation.walkthrough: The chat abbreviation is taken whole, so the phrase is a source of letters, not a description.
explanation.definitionFit: To loll is to lie or lounge in a relaxed, lazy way, much as one sprawls.

clue.text: Start to burn coal, ditching oil at last

indicators.note: to ditch something is to throw it away, so the letter is removed

parts.note: lignite is soft brown coal

indicators.note: at last points to the final position, so only the end letter is meant

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Firing up a coal stove after finally giving up on oil heating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start to burn' looks like it might take a first letter of 'burn', but it is the whole definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignite is to catch fire or set something alight, the moment burning begins.

clue.text: Dutch painter apparently covering room with new gloss

indicators.note: covering one thing with another hides the first under the second, so one piece stands in for another

parts.note: Johannes Vermeer was a Dutch painter
RM is the abbreviation for room
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: An Old Master seemingly painting over a room with a fresh glossy coat.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviation for room is replaced inside the painter's name by the one for new.
explanation.definitionFit: A veneer is a thin attractive surface layer, and figuratively a superficial gloss hiding what lies beneath.

clue.text: Stays gracious and formal

parts.note: cor! is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'good gracious!'
set means fixed or prescribed, as in a set form

explanation.surface: Someone remains polite and correct in their manners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stays' looks like a verb meaning remains; it is the old noun for a boned undergarment.
explanation.definitionFit: Stays is the traditional name for a stiffened bodice laced round the torso, an older word for the same garment.

clue.text: Ballet expert to choose girl to dance

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and end up in new positions

parts.note: the letters as printed

explanation.surface: A ballet master picking out a young woman to perform.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's casting director is just a source of letters, and the dancing is the shuffle signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A choreologist records and studies dance movement using a notation system, a specialist in the art of ballet.

clue.text: Guests' whimsies on a regular basis, leading to tumble?

indicators.note: something done regularly happens at fixed intervals, so every other letter is used

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and so on letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Visitors' playful fancies, indulged often, ending in someone falling over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tumble' suggests a fall, but in slang to tumble to something is to realise it; the question mark flags that stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: To tumble to a trick is to suddenly understand it, the same as catching on or becoming aware.

clue.text: Breaking law, can lose benefits

indicators.note: a broken object shatters into fragments that may be reassembled in another order

parts.note: the letters as printed

explanation.surface: A warning that lawbreakers may forfeit their welfare payments.
explanation.walkthrough: The three words make a plausible threat, which hides that their letters are the answer rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Allowances are sums paid out regularly, such as state payments, just as benefits are.

clue.text: Competent guy embracing dad

indicators.note: to embrace is to wrap one's arms around, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: a guy is a rope or wire that braces a mast or tent, so a cable
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A skilled man giving his father a hug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man, which fits the hug, but it is a supporting rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Capable and competent both describe someone with the skill and ability to do a job well.

clue.text: Moving home, oddly sneers at one old inn

parts.note: a caravan is a home on wheels that can be moved

indicators.note: oddly means taking the odd-numbered positions, the first, third, fifth and so on

parts.note: the odd-placed letters of these two words
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone relocating, who strangely scoffs at a historic pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving home' sounds like relocating, but it is a noun phrase for a mobile home.
explanation.definitionFit: A caravanserai was a roadside inn with a courtyard where travelling merchants rested in Asia and North Africa.

clue.text: Insult full of emotion causes estrangement

indicators.note: something full of a thing holds it inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: to diss someone is to insult them
affect is the psychological term for emotion or feeling

explanation.surface: An emotionally charged slur drives people apart.
explanation.walkthrough: Affect, stressed on the first syllable, is the psychologist's noun for feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: To disaffect people is to alienate them, turning loyalty into resentment, which is estranging them.

clue.text: Haydn almost battered poet

indicators.note: something battered has been knocked about and bent out of its shape

parts.note: the letters as printed, every one used

explanation.surface: The composer Haydn nearly beaten up by a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' wants to cut the composer's name short, but it is fodder, and every letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Dylan Thomas was the Welsh writer of 'Do not go gentle into that good night' and Under Milk Wood.

clue.text: Orchid spray spilled all over the place

indicators.note: things scattered all over the place are in disarray and out of order

parts.note: the letters as printed

explanation.surface: A flower spray knocked over, petals scattered everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: A spray is a bunch of flowers, which suits the orchid, but here it supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The lady's slipper is a wild orchid with a pouch-shaped lip resembling a shoe.

clue.text: Heard sardonic arguments in corners of square

indicators.note: what is heard is taken by ear, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

parts.note: wry means sardonic and tangles are disputes

explanation.surface: Bitter, sarcastic disputes overheard in the corners of a town square.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, the two words run together; the T moves across the word break.
explanation.definitionFit: Each corner of a square is ninety degrees, so its four corners are all angles of that kind.

clue.text: Doctor first heals relative

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it and alter its arrangement

parts.note: the letters as printed

explanation.surface: A physician treats a family member before anyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' reads as a physician, which suits 'heals', but it is a verb telling you to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-sister shares one parent with you, so she is a family member.

clue.text: Introverts love being in railway society

indicators.note: something being in another is placed inside it

parts.note: the LNER was the London and North Eastern Railway
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
S is the abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: Shy people in love join a railway enthusiasts' club.
explanation.walkthrough: The LNER is one of Britain's old railway companies, and its initials are the standard crossword railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Loners prefer their own company, much as introverts are people who find solitude restful.

clue.text: Writing note over letter without any resistance

indicators.note: without any of something means every instance of it goes

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for note
taken as written
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Penning a note on a letter without any opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' looks like a positional instruction but is taken literally, and both R's go from the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A novelette is a short novel or long story, a piece of written fiction.

clue.text: Commander-in-Chief with programming language for drone producer

parts.note: CIC is the abbreviation for Commander-in-Chief
Ada is a computer programming language

explanation.surface: A military chief using software to build unmanned aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drone' suggests an unmanned aircraft, which fits the military picture, but it is a droning noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Male cicadas make a loud, sustained buzzing hum, so the insect generates a constant droning sound.

clue.text: Babies annoy anti-social type

parts.note: a litter is a set of young born together
to bug someone is to annoy them

explanation.surface: Infants irritate an unsociable person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Babies' suggests human infants, but here it is a litter of puppies or kittens.
explanation.definitionFit: A litterbug drops rubbish in public places, behaviour that is inconsiderate to the community.

clue.text: Netting wound over top of shrubs as protection against aphids?

indicators.note: in a down answer, being over something means sitting above it, so the order is fixed

parts.note: lace is an openwork netted fabric
to wing someone is to wound them slightly, as with a bullet

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A gardener drapes mesh over bushes to keep greenfly off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound' looks like the past tense of wind, as netting wound round a bush, but it is an injury verb. The question mark marks the definition as playful.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacewing insects and their larvae prey heavily on greenfly, so gardeners welcome them as natural pest control.

clue.text: PM of Middle Eastern country supporting Democrat

indicators.note: in a down answer, what supports something holds it up from below, so it comes second

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for Democrat
Israeli means of or from Israel

explanation.surface: A Middle Eastern prime minister backing an American Democrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PM of Middle Eastern country' reads as a foreign leader; only 'PM' is the definition, and it means a British one.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Disraeli served twice as British Prime Minister in the nineteenth century under Queen Victoria.

clue.text: Eggs on northern star

indicators.note: in an across answer, sitting on another means following it

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for northern
ova is the Latin plural for eggs

explanation.surface: Urging on a celebrity from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eggs on' reads as encourages, but 'Eggs' is a noun and 'on' places it.
explanation.definitionFit: A nova is a star that suddenly flares to great brightness before fading.

clue.text: Frenchmen and I dissent furiously about a removal of rights

indicators.note: about means around, so the result is wrapped round a single letter
acting furiously means flailing wildly, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man and some angry Frenchmen protest about being stripped of their rights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And' joins the first two words as letter supply rather than linking definition to wordplay; the shuffled letters then go round the single A.
explanation.definitionFit: Disenfranchisement is depriving someone of a right, especially the right to vote.

clue.text: Massive blokes invading one's space "discontentedly"

indicators.note: an invader pushes its way inside, so one part goes into another

parts.note: one's, read as one is, is I'm
blokes is British slang for men

indicators.note: dis-contented means with its contents taken out, so only the outer letters stay

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Huge men barging into someone's personal space, to their annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks flag 'discontentedly' as a pun: not unhappily, but with its contents removed. 'One's' is read as 'one is', giving I'm.
explanation.definitionFit: Immense means extremely large or huge in size, so it is a synonym of great bulk.

clue.text: Less original story swallowed by senior

indicators.note: what is swallowed ends up inside the swallower

parts.note: SR is the abbreviation for senior
a tale is a story

explanation.surface: An old person falls for a tired, unoriginal yarn.
explanation.walkthrough: Swallowing a story usually means believing it, but here it is literal insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Stale means hackneyed and worn out, so staler describes something with less freshness or novelty.

clue.text: English composer ultimately made poor case for piece

parts.note: Gustav Holst was the English composer of The Planets

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so the final letters are taken

parts.note: the last letter of each word

explanation.surface: An English composer eventually wrote a weak argument in favour of a musical piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece' sounds like a musical work, but in slang it is a gun, and 'case for' reads as an argument when it is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A holster is the leather sheath worn on a belt to carry a handgun, which slang calls a piece.

clue.text: Political enforcer saying this inflicts cuts

parts.note: a whip enforces party discipline in parliament
a saw is an old saying or proverb

explanation.surface: A party whip announces that this policy imposes spending cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuts' suggests budget reductions, fitting the political scene, but they are literal cuts made by a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A whipsaw is a narrow-bladed saw in a frame, a cutting tool, so it literally makes cuts.

clue.text: Cultivated grass with passion

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for with
heat means intensity of feeling, as in the heat of the moment

explanation.surface: A lawn tended with real love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cultivated grass' sounds like a lawn, but cereal crops are botanically grasses.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheat is a cereal plant of the grass family grown as a farm crop for its grain.

clue.text: President of India introduced to foolish boy

indicators.note: something introduced to another is put into it

parts.note: mad means foolish, and a son is a boy
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: The Indian head of state is presented to a silly lad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'President of India' reads as one title, but 'of' only links; James Madison was the fourth US president.
explanation.definitionFit: James Madison served as the fourth President of the United States, a founding father of the constitution.

clue.text: Time to break young horse

indicators.note: to break into something is to force a way inside it

parts.note: seed means offspring or descendants
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: It is the moment to tame a foal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break' is used of training a young horse, but here it means split open; 'young' is a noun, not an adjective for the horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A steed is a literary word for a horse, especially one that is ridden.

clue.text: Camel tottered, moving treasure hunter's gear

indicators.note: things that are moving shift position and settle in a new order

parts.note: the letters as printed

explanation.surface: A camel staggers along under an explorer's equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tottered, moving' both suggest the camel's gait; only 'moving' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal detector is the electronic device people sweep over ground when searching for buried coins and treasure.

clue.text: Matchless version of rap online

indicators.note: a version of something is a reworked form of it

parts.note: the letters as printed

explanation.surface: An unbeatable rap track released on the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface praises a song, but its last two words simply supply the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonpareil means having no equal, from French for without a peer, so it means unrivalled.

clue.text: Stem of asparagus with excellent herb

parts.note: an asparagus spear is the edible stem
mint means in perfect condition

explanation.surface: Asparagus served with a fine herb, a recipe suggestion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stem of' looks like an instruction to take the first letter, but it is the vegetable's spear.
explanation.definitionFit: Spearmint is a common garden mint used in cooking and flavouring, a culinary plant.

clue.text: Theatre is sued after shrinking further publication

indicators.note: once a phrase has shrunk, only an inner stretch of it is left, losing letters at both ends

parts.note: the letters run across the three words once the outer ones are trimmed away

explanation.surface: A theatre faces a lawsuit after cutting back its operations.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits in theat-RE IS SUE-d; 'shrinking' reads as a theatre downsizing, but it trims letters from both ends of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A reissue is a book or record brought out again, a fresh printing or release.

clue.text: Going west, overdrawn nation finally loses credit

indicators.note: in an across answer, west is to the left, so the letters read right to left

parts.note: OD is the bank statement abbreviation for overdrawn
the UK is a nation

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so only the last letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A country in debt heading downhill eventually loses its credit rating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Credit' looks financial, matching the debt, but it means praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Kudos is praise and honour for an achievement, the credit someone is given.
